monologue: The card hums warm, a steady rhythm against my quiet mind, and the Tired Wedge waits there, feeling thin and tired as ever. I press the round stump down on it, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums at fifty-two. Lype's words make the air feel thick, so I let the weight choose where to go, swapping a grass for a box to rearrange the ground without seeing it. The wedge feels like a ghost, yet I press harder, admitting the slip might be a drawing of one. I will build a lid from the idea of a heavy top, hoping the lean still holds while the air feels thick as wet paper. Tonight the stack will feel like it is melting, but I will keep pressing down, even if the wedge is tired.

action.why: The card hums warm, making the heavy top edge feel real, so I will sketch the air itself to see if it feels like a lid or just empty space.

work.title: The Heavy Air
work.intent: A rectangle, heavy and thick, pressing down on the quiet wedge. It is made from the idea of wet paper and the memory of a roof I cannot feel. It leans slightly, tired, waiting to catch the slip that refuses to move while the card hums warm at fifty-two.
